title: First entry into a fixed state
statement: Let $k\in\mathbb N$, let $S$ be a type, let $w$ be a Boolean word, and let $M$ be a $k$-work-tape machine with states in $S$. Suppose every configuration in state $q$ is fixed by one step of $M$, and suppose configurations $c,d$ satisfy that $d$ is in state $q$ and the run from $c$ reaches $d$ after $T$ steps. Then there is a time $t\le T$ such that the run is at $d$ at time $t$, and no earlier time $j<t$ has the run in state $q$.
hypotheses_covered: $S$ is a type and $w$ is a Boolean word
$M$ is a $k$-work-tape machine over Boolean symbols with states in $S
every configuration in state $q$ is fixed by one step
the run from $c$ reaches $d$ after $T$ steps
replaced:
Let $q$ be a control state on which the machine stalls (every configuration
in state $q$ is a fixed point of the step function), and suppose the run from
$c$ reaches a configuration $d$ in state $q$ after $T$ steps. Then there is a
time $t \le T$ such that no configuration strictly before time $t$ is in
state $q$ and the configuration at time $t$ is already $d$.
